The new circular issued by BCI Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra within hours of the earlier communication states that members of the BCI debated the move to halt enrolments. "After thorough discussion the Members are of the unanimous view that as per the latest report, vast majority of the students of NALSAR (2026 pass out students) are innocent and they were not inclined to take part in the move of disrespect. Accordingly, the Council modifies the order of Chairman with regard to the ban on the enrolment of the NALSAR Students with the State Bar Councils. All the students will be entitled to get enrolled with the State Bar Councils of their choice," the BCI said. BCI Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra Mishra had earlier asked NALSAR Vice-Chancellor Prof Srikrishna Deva Rao and all state bar councils to submit a report on the persons instrumental in initiating, organising, or mobilising the campaign. In another attempt, a fake google executive id was used to intimidate publishers. The murky operation, which is slowly coming to light, was carried out several months before the centre got relief from the Supreme Court. Accepting the submissions of the Special Investigation Team (SIT), the apex court had on September 15 given a clean chit to the animal rescue and rehabilitation centre. Spread over 3,000 acres within Reliance’s Jamnagar refinery complex, Vantara has been projected as one of the largest private animal care facilities in the world. While concluding that Vantara had complied with all legal requirements, especially during the acquisition of animals, the Supreme Court also told Vantara that it can pursue legal remedies against misinformation or defamation, and any such cases will be decided on merit. items.title: A day inside a Delhi SIR camp: Forms, confusion and long days
items.summary: Delhi is currently undergoing the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, with the Election Commission extending the deadline to submit forms to August 17. Booth Level Officers are handling everything from distributing and collecting forms to digitising the data. To make the process easier, some local residents have set up small camps in their homes to help people fill out and submit their forms. We visited one such camp, where voters faced several challenges in understanding and completing the process. For many, SIR has emerged as a confusing exercise. Some also expressed fears that they could lose their citizenship because of the process. The term ‘relative’ used in the form has added to the confusion, with voters, volunteers, and even some polling officials unsure about how it should be interpreted. Abida, who is unhappy with the government and no longer votes, came to the camp after people told her that failing to fill out the form could get her expelled from Delhi. “Even if I fill out the form, will you stop the demolition?” she asked us. items.title: Superstition vs. Constitution: Supreme Court upholds life term of man who killed woman accused of witchcraft
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday upheld the life sentence of a man convicted of murdering a woman over allegations that she practised witchcraft. [ Balku Oram v. State of Odisha ] A Bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and NV Anjaria held that the trial court and the Orissa High Court had correctly held the accused guilty and that his conviction and sentence deserved to be affirmed. The Court said the direct evidence on record clearly established the role of the accused and the co-accused in the killing. "The nature of the direct evidence appearing against the appellant (Balku Oram) is compelling, which clearly establishes that the appellant with the co-accused brutally murdered the deceased on the allegation of her causing death of the youngest daughter of Manobodha Naik by practicing witchcraft," the Court said. Justice PK Mishra and Justice NV Anjaria The Court also expressed concern over the continuing practice of witch-hunting and how superstitions continue to prevail over rule of law. items.title: Advocates acting as insolvency professionals liable to collect, deposit GST: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has ruled that advocates acting as insolvency professionals are liable to collect Goods and Services Tax (GST) from recipients of their services and deposit it with the government under the forward charge mechanism [Kanwal Chaudhary v. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India]. A Division Bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Shail Jain held that advocates providing insolvency and receivership services must obtain GST registration and comply with the requirements applicable to insolvency professionals as a class. “ An Advocate acting as an Insolvency Professional would, therefore, be governed by the ‘forward charge mechanism’, which is applicable to Insolvency Professionals, as a class, and not by the ‘reverse charge mechanism’, which is otherwise applicable to Advocates rendering legal services ,” the Court said. Justice Prathiba Singh and Justice Shail Jain Under the forward charge mechanism, the service provider adds GST to the invoice, collects it from the recipient and deposits it with the government. Under reverse charge, the recipient of the service is responsible for depositing GST. The Court clarified that its ruling applies only to services rendered

items.title: Tamil Nadu: Nine-year-old girl allegedly sexually assaulted while walking home
items.summary: A nine-year-old Class 4 student was allegedly sexually assaulted by an unidentified man while she was walking home in Denkanikottai in Tamil Nadu’s Krishnagiri district on the evening of August 12, Wednesday. The child was walking home with three other children, but the three reached their homes before her, leaving her alone when the alleged assault took place, according to police. The incident was reported around 1 am on Thursday after the child’s mother lodged a complaint with the Denkanikottai All Women Police Station (AWPS). Police have registered an FIR under Section 87 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) (kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc) and Section 5(6) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. The child was taken to Krishnagiri Government Hospital for a medical examination. Police said the examination will help determine whether a sexual assault took place. A police team has also visited the scene and is collecting evidence and other information as part of the investigation. The child does not know the identity of the alleged accused, but has told police that she would be able to identify him.

Justice Viju Abraham briefly took up the matter today, when the State's counsel was asked to get instructions. “ For such issue, should there be a suspension is the question … You can go on with the disciplinary proceedings… but can suspension be a punishment (in such matters)?" " Government Pleader shall apprise the Court of the specific reasons for which the petitioner was suspended ," the Court added in its order. items.title: Why four people went on hunger strike against NEET in Chennai | The News Minute
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu Assembly on August 11, passed a resolution urging the Union government to abolish NEET, citing concerns over irregularities in the examination, dependence on coaching centres and the impact on students. The resolution came as four members of the Anti-NEET Federation were completing an indefinite hunger strike in Chennai. The protest ended on August 12, after the Assembly passed the resolution, seeking not only the abolition of NEET but also greater control for states over education. In this ground report, TNM’s Nithesh Kumar speaks to members of the Anti-NEET Federation, including Anitha’s brother S Manirathinam, to understand why the movement continues to demand the complete abolition of NEET, and why the debate over the exam remains closely tied to questions of education and equality.
